plan: In a second-price auction (pay second-highest bid if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds both competitors' bids (guaranteeing non-negative profit) and lose otherwise, avoiding overpaying. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no incentive to shade up or down. With no prior history in this single-round game, I'll bid my true value of $25 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. Bidding your value ensures you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying. My value is $17, so I will bid exactly that.

In this second-price auction format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid between my value and my inflated bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With value = $39, I should bid $39 to maximize expected profit.
